examples.scenario: Publicly accessible AWS S3 bucket leaks sensitive internal documents due to overly permissive bucket policy allowing anonymous read access.

technical_data.curl_http_request:
curl -I https://confidential-corp-docs.s3.amazonaws.com/hr/employee_salaries.csv
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-amz-id-2: 2N1vWnWqkG9t3Xvo5l2JxB1R6RzS5M9qE5u3yLz0Q5y6fJ9+7X9+9Z5s7R0E1W2V
x-amz-request-id: 3A1D2D4E5F6G7H8I
Date: Tue, 23 May 2024 15:00:00 GMT
Last-Modified: Sun, 19 May 2024 13:45:23 GMT
ETag: "1f3870be274f6c49b3e31a0c6728957f"
Accept-Ranges: bytes
Content-Type: text/csv
Content-Length: 10240
Server: AmazonS3

indicators: Anonymous access logged in CloudTrail with userIdentity.type = "Anonymous"
Sensitive file names such as hr/employee_salaries.csv and internal-financials/Q3_report.xlsx publicly accessible
HTTP 200 OK responses to unauthenticated GET requests
examples.detection_method: Automated periodic scans using AWS Config rules and third-party tools (e.g., ScoutSuite) to detect buckets with public-read policies. Monitoring CloudTrail logs for GetObject events with anonymous principal. Alerting on unusual data downloads from storage buckets. Enabling S3 server access logs and analyzing for external IP addresses retrieving sensitive files.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1110 - Brute Force (if attacker brute forces credentials later)

examples.scenario: Azure Blob storage container configured with 'Container (anonymous read access for containers and blobs)' public access level exposing internal backup archives.

technical_data.azure_cli_public_access_check:
az storage container show --account-name corpbackupstorage --name internal-backups --query publicAccess
"container"
technical_data.sample_http_request_and_response:
GET https://corpbackupstorage.blob.core.windows.net/internal-backups/2023-12-31-backup.zip HTTP/1.1
Host: corpbackupstorage.blob.core.windows.net


HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 104857600
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Last-Modified: Wed, 31 Dec 2023 23:59:59 GMT
x-ms-blob-type: BlockBlob
x-ms-request-id: 7a8b9c0d-e01e-0023-1234-56789abcdef0
x-ms-version: 2021-04-10
Date: Tue, 23 May 2024 16:30:00 GMT

[Binary content of backup zip file]

indicators: Container public access level set to 'Container' (anonymous read access for blobs and container metadata)
Anonymous HTTP GET requests returning 200 OK with backup archive files
Azure activity logs showing GetBlob operations from unknown external IPs
Absence of SAS tokens or OAuth authorization headers in blob access requests
examples.detection_method: Use Azure Security Center recommendations to detect public access on blob containers. Enable Azure Monitor logs for Storage Analytics and review access patterns. Use Azure Policy to enforce private containers and block public access. Scan containers with tools like AzScanner or Blobfuse with detection scripts for public ACLs.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1071.001 - Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
T1496 - Resource Hijacking (if attacker uploads malicious blobs)

examples.scenario: Misconfigured Google Cloud Storage bucket allows unauthenticated users to list and read bucket contents, exposing source code and credentials files.

technical_data.gsutil_ls_command:
$ gsutil ls gs://corp-source-code/
gs://corp-source-code/main.py
gs://corp-source-code/config.json
gs://corp-source-code/credentials.yaml
technical_data.curl_unauthenticated_request:
curl -i https://storage.googleapis.com/corp-source-code/config.json
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
Content-Length: 256
Last-Modified: Thu, 22 May 2024 12:00:00 GMT
ETag: "abc123def456"

{
  "db_host": "10.0.0.5",
  "db_user": "admin",
  "db_password": "SuperSecretPass123!",
  "api_key": "AIzaSyD-EXAMPLEKEY1234567890"
}

indicators: IAM policy binding includes 'allUsers' with roles/storage.objectViewer
Unauthenticated HTTP GET requests successfully retrieving sensitive files like config.json and credentials.yaml
Audit logs showing storage.objects.get requests without authenticated principal
Presence of plaintext credentials and API keys in publicly accessible JSON files
examples.detection_method: Regular IAM policy audits using gcloud commands or Security Command Center. Automated scanning with tools like Forseti Security or GCloud Bucket Auditor to detect public IAM bindings. Enable and analyze Cloud Audit Logs for unauthenticated access to storage objects. Use Data Loss Prevention (DLP) tools to scan bucket contents for secrets.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials in Files
